name: Abiram
overview: Abiram was a male biblical figure known as the firstborn son of Hiel. His life is notably marked by his death during the rebuilding of Jericho, an event that highlights the consequences of disobedience to God’s commands. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Abiram means '[my] father is exalted,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name. This meaning does not indicate that the name was given directly by God but carries significance in its expression of honor toward the father.
familyAndRelationships: Abiram is explicitly identified as the son of Hiel. Beyond this relationship, Scripture does not provide further family details or connections for Abiram.
scriptureSignificance: Abiram's significance in Scripture lies in his death as a direct consequence of his father Hiel’s attempt to rebuild Jericho, a city previously destroyed by divine command. His death serves as a solemn reminder of the seriousness of adhering to God's instructions and the judgment that follows disobedience. This event underscores the faithfulness required of God’s people and the consequences when His will is disregarded.
